name: TN-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent DesJarlais running with large financial edge
Democratic challenger underfunded with minimal cash
model.rationale: The district's R+11 lean, DesJarlais's incumbency and roughly nine-to-one fundraising advantage, and prediction markets pricing a Republican win near 95% all point the same direction. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays close to the baseline Republican margin.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending targeting DesJarlais's personal-history vulnerabilities could tighten the race, though the district lean makes an upset unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TN-04 is a solidly Republican southern Tennessee seat with an R+11 partisan lean, and incumbent Scott DesJarlais is seeking another term. He holds a decisive financial advantage, having raised about $537,000 with roughly $495,000 on hand, while Democratic nominee Victoria Broderick has raised under $60,000 and reports only about $8,500 in cash. Two independent candidates are on the ballot but lack significant resources.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price a Republican win at roughly 95%. The expected margin is a comfortable Republican victory in the mid-teens, with the incumbent favored but not fully immune to surprise.
